To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phase separation of AlGaN grown by MOCPD is suppressed by optimizing the Al precursor supply and the AlGaN strain is modified by varying the thickness of the AlN IL inserted between the AlGaN and the GaN layer.

the inhomogeneity of Al compositions in AlGaN epitaxy was suppressed by optimizing the gas flow rates and that the residual strain in AlxGa1-xN/GaN induced by the lattice mismatch was modulated by inserting a high temperature (TH) AlN interfacial layer between the AlxGa1−xN and GaN layers, which resulted in the improvement of crystalline qualities and Al-incorporations into the AlxGa 1−xN layer.

the inhomogeneous distributions of the Al composition in both the vertical (Al composition gradient) and the lateral growth direction (lateral Al composition fluctuation) can be suppressed by optimizing the gas flow rate ratio of TMAl to TMG, and the residual strain in AlN IL/AlGaN/GaN structure can be modulated by varying AlN IL thickness to improve the crystallinity of AlGaN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth of high crystalline quality Al x Ga1−x N epitaxial layers by MOCVD and their use in HEMTs.
the improvement of the AlGN/GaN epitaxy quality by controlling the gas-phase pre-reactions of Al precursors and the residual strain of AlGaN/GaN.
the growth of high-quality AlGaN films and the fabrication of AlGaN/GaNGaN HEMT structures with excellent electrical performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a combination of the phase separation-suppressed AlGaN growth by the optimization of growth conditions and strain-modulated AlGaN growth using an HT AlN IL is a very effective way to obtain a high crystalline quality Al-rich AlGaN film.

a high crystalline quality Al 0.25 Ga 0.75 N layer can be obtained on GaN templates with an AlGaN thickness of 1000 nm, and a high Al composition of 30% in AlGaN layers is achievable with a 100 nm HT AlN IL.

the growth conditions were optimized to suppress the gas-phase pre-reactions, the strain was modulated by the HT AlN IL, and the crystalline quality of the AlGn/GaN HEMTs was improved by the strain modification
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystalline quality of the AlGN epitaxial layer is strongly dependent on the residual strain in AlN/GaN and the inhomogeneous distribution of Al composition in the AlGaN layer.
the crystalline quality of the AlGnAs layer is improved by suppressing phase separation and modulating strain.
a high quality AlGaN/GaNGaN heterostructure can be grown with MOCVD by suppressing the phase separation and modulating the residual strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AlGaN/GaN HEMT structure can be optimized by controlling the residual strain in AlN IL.

the crystalline quality of the AlGN layer can be significantly improved by suppressing the inhomogeneous Al composition distributions in both the vertical growth direction and the in-plane lateral growth direction and modulating the residual strain in AlN IL.
the AlGaN/GaN heterostructure can be improved by controlling the AlGaN layer growth conditions and inserting a HT AlN IL with an optimized thickness.
